text:
Maria: Heads up — we need a clear event shape for audit logs that covers both console actions and API-driven changes (routing policies, quota edits, rollouts). Compliance wants exports that let them answer "which identity caused this change" reliably.
Aj: Agree. trick is when changes come from service accounts, keys, or CI bots. We should add actor_kind and orig_auth_context.
Sam: +1. Minimal fields I care about: event_id, ts, resource_type, resource_id, change_summary, actor_id, actor_kind, actor_display, auth_method, pre_state_digest, post_state_digest.
Nina: Do we need full pre/post deltas in the export? Compliance said they want diffs but also need storage sizing estimates. Deltas can be huge.
Maria: Diffs optional but provide a diff_url reference. For exports we can include compact ndjson with hashes and a separate attachable diff blob (gz). That keeps stream small.
Alex: Example event shape suggestion (NDJSON line):
{"event_id":"e-123","ts":"2026-03-10T15:02:30Z","resource":"routing_policy","resource_id":"rp-45","action":"update","actor_id":"u-789","actor_kind":"human","actor_display":"Aj Patel","auth_method":"sso:okta","change_summary":"scaled route weight 20->50","pre_hash":"sha256:abcd","post_hash":"sha256:ef01","diff_url":"s3://redwood-audit/diffs/e-123.gz"}
infra-bot: deploy bot: exported 2026-03-10T15:05:00Z — export job id ex-20260310-1
Aj: One tricky part — API keys used by customers for their own infra will appear as actor_kind=api_key and actor_id = key-xxx. Do we resolve the owning user/org? We need both token_id and resolved_owner to satisfy forensic requests.
Sam: We should include both token_id and resolved_subject. token_id lets security link usage to a credential; resolved_subject (user or service account) is for human attribution. Keep both optional fields.
Nina: Privacy: any field that can hold PII (actor_display, resolved_subject.email) needs redaction options. Export profile should support pii_level: none|display|full.
Maria: Good call. Default export for auditors = display, but legal eDiscovery can request full with approvals and audit trail.
Alex: Streaming vs batch: streaming (kinesis/pubsub) gives near-rt for SIEM, but batch NDJSON export is simpler for long-term retention and downstream ingestion. We should support both. Export API:
POST /internal/audit/export
body: {"range_start":"2026-03-09T00:00Z","range_end":"2026-03-10T00:00Z","format":"ndjson","pii_level":"display","delivery":{"type":"s3","bucket":"acct-zzz-audit"}}
compliance-bot: note — retention defaults to 7 years for enterprise, configurable by org. Encryption-at-rest mandatory.
Aj: For attribution resolution we need a service that maps auth_context -> actor (e.g., api_key -> owner, jwt sub -> user). It must be idempotent and deterministic; include resolver_version on events.
Sam: Add resolver_version and actor_resolution_ts to event shape.
Maria: Also include change_scope: ui|api|infra for quick filtering (eg: ui for console changes, api for public API, infra for internal systems).
Alex: UX ask from console: when you view a policy in the UI, show latest actor and a one-click export for that resource history. We need an internal route to fetch events by resource_id fast.
Nina: Performance note: we should index by resource_id + ts and store a compact timeline. For NDJSON export we can stream query results directly to S3 with gz.
Aj: Edge case: automated rollouts that touch hundreds of policies — collapse into a rollup event with children ids, else auditors drown.
Maria: Let's draft a proposal for the exact schema, export API, and retention/PII modes. Volunteers? Aj + Sam to sketch shape, Nina + infra to outline export impl, Maria to consolidate and run by legal.
Aj: I can start a PR with schema v1 in the repo — will ping when ready. :thumbsup:
Sam: I'll write test harness for resolver and sample exports.
infra-bot: note — created ticket INFRA-2398 export pipeline spike
Maria: Thanks team. We'll iterate. :eyes:
